title: Redis Memory Management
description: Optimize Redis memory usage with eviction policies, key expiration, memory-efficient encodings, and monitoring techniques.

data.text: Because Redis stores everything in RAM, memory is the most common bottleneck. Learning how Redis manages memory lets you cache more data safely and avoid out-of-memory crashes.

Set `maxmemory` to limit the total dataset size. When Redis reaches this limit, it applies an eviction policy to decide which keys to remove. Choosing the right policy depends on whether your keys have TTLs and whether you want to protect hot data.

rows: Data stores where every write must succeed
Pure caches with or without TTL
Evict LRU among keys with TTL
Caches where only some keys expire

data.title: Set memory limits in redis.conf
data.content: Cap memory at 2 GB and use allkeys-lru eviction.

data.text: Redis automatically re-encodes values to save memory. Small lists, sets, and hashes use compact encodings. You can encourage efficient encoding by limiting collection sizes and using small numeric IDs instead of long strings.

data.title: Check object encoding in Node.js
data.content: Use ioredis to inspect how Redis stores a key internally.

data.title: Monitor before tuning
data.text: Always inspect Redis with INFO memory and MEMORY USAGE before changing policies. Premature eviction tuning can evict hot cache data and degrade latency.

data.title: Tactics to control memory growth
items: Assign TTLs to every cache key so Redis can reuse memory naturally.
Use `volatile-lru` or `volatile-ttl` if some keys must never expire.
Avoid storing large blobs in Redis; use object storage for files or images.
Split hot and cold datasets across separate Redis instances.

data.caption: Redis memory eviction decision flow
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Write request] --> B{At maxmemory?}
    B -->|No| C[Accept write]
    B -->|Yes| D{Eviction policy?}
    D -->|noeviction| E[Reject write]
    D -->|allkeys-lru| F[Evict LRU key]
    D -->|volatile-lru| G[Evict LRU among TTL keys]
    D -->|allkeys-random| H[Evict random key]
    F --> C
    G --> C
    H --> C

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Set maxmemory and choose an eviction policy that matches your data lifecycle.
Use TTLs and Redis auto-encoding to keep memory usage predictable.
Monitor with INFO memory and MEMORY USAGE before scaling hardware.
